annotation.title_clean: Views of the Islamic Republic of Iran on Resolution 79/239 of the General Assembly "Artificial Intelligence in the military domain and its implications for international peace and security"
annotation.title_en: Views of the Islamic Republic of Iran on Resolution 79/239 of the General Assembly "Artificial Intelligence in the military domain and its implications for international peace and security"
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Islamic Republic of Iran (Government submission to UN Secretary-General)
annotation.venue: UN Office for Disarmament Affairs documents library (General Assembly First Committee, 80th session)
annotation.summary_en: Iran's national submission to the UN Secretary-General on UNGA Resolution 79/239 on military AI. It favours exclusively peaceful AI use, UN-centred consensus-based regulation preserving state sovereignty, legally binding instruments, avoiding an AI divide, and replacing 'responsible application' with 'peaceful application'.
key_provisions_or_claims: Supports exclusively peaceful application of AI; regulatory authority is the sovereign prerogative of states.
Regulation must be inclusive and UN consensus-based to prevent a Digital Divide becoming an AI Divide.
Premature to assert full applicability of international, humanitarian and human rights law to AI; legal framework may need adaptation.
Prefers legally binding arrangements over norm-setting or political instruments.
Rejects 'responsible application' as vague; proposes 'peaceful application' instead.
